solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fabric provides a covering on side of bed

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it, so the covering comes after
one side of the word bed is its final letter, the edge it ends on

parts.note: a mask is a covering for the face

explanation.surface: A furnishing tip: some cloth gives a protective cover along the edge of a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side of' takes the last letter of 'bed', D, and 'on' puts A MASK after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven textile, often silk or linen, so it is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Film with terrible score, awful opus

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of zero, the worst possible

indicators.note: awful signals that the letters of opus are jumbled

explanation.surface: A critic panning a movie with a dreadful soundtrack and a ghastly musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks musical, alongside 'opus', but is a batsman's tally. 'awful' rearranges OPUS to SOUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck Soup is a 1933 Marx Brothers comedy movie.

clue.text: Man perhaps taken in by idiotic fool

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other, so the island sits within the word for idiotic

parts.note: mad means crazy, foolish
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man, it seems, has been conned by some idiotic fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool someone is to deceive them, lead them astray.

clue.text: Stop everyone going beyond street

indicators.note: going beyond means coming after, so the word for everyone follows

parts.note: all means every person

explanation.surface: An order for everybody to halt rather than go past the end of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: When an engine cuts out it stops; to stall also means to halt progress.

clue.text: Make shrill sound meeting Regina or Rex?

definitions.text: Make shrill sound meeting Regina or Rex?

parts.note: to whistle is to make a high shrill noise
R is the abbreviation for both Regina (queen) and Rex (king)

explanation.surface: Someone shrilling a whistle on meeting a king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a whistler makes shrill sounds, and Rex Whistler was a British painter, which the question mark hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: One who produces piercing piped notes, and also the surname of the artist Rex Whistler.

clue.text: I go with men, hoping somehow one will know the way back

definitions.text: one will know the way back

indicators.note: somehow suggests these letters are worked into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone sets off with a group of men, hoping one of them can find the route home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges I GO, MEN and HOPING; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing birds of this kind are trained to fly back to their loft from far away.

clue.text: One of us may be in and out of Oxford

definitions.text: One of us may be in and out of Oxford

parts.words: One of us may be in and out of Oxford
parts.note: an Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe; its laces thread in and out of the eyelets

explanation.surface: Members of a group boast of coming and going from Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the city or university but is the Oxford shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cords used to tie footwear weave through its holes, as on an Oxford.

clue.text: Drunkard Henry bumps into lion in the country

indicators.note: bumping into here means getting inside, so the drunk and Henry go within the lion

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
a sot is a habitual drunk
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A drunk called Henry stumbles into a lion somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like rural land but is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small landlocked kingdom surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Embarrassed-looking individual performed again

parts.note: an embarrassed face flushes red
one means a single person

explanation.surface: A blushing person had to repeat a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done a second time has been repeated, carried out once more.

clue.text: One of the top actors rendering Shakespearean bumpkin endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the bumpkin's name is dropped

parts.note: Costard is the rustic clown in Love's Labour's Lost

explanation.surface: A leading actor is playing a Shakespearean yokel, but not quite to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from COSTARD, Shakespeare's clown.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star shares top billing with another leading performer in a film or play.

clue.text: English male told what to do, moulded into shape?

parts.note: bossed means ordered about

explanation.surface: An Englishman ordered about and pressed into conformity.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that embossing raises a design rather than moulding a whole object.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossed metal or paper has been pressed so that a raised pattern stands out.

clue.text: Someone known to have nicely old-fashioned African party in a church

indicators.note: in places the old-fashioned word and the party inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
quaint means attractively old-fashioned
the ANC is the African National Congress of South Africa

explanation.surface: A contact described as charmingly dated, attending an African political gathering in a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: An acquaintance is a person one knows slightly, not a close friend.

clue.text: Add I can't, but …? I may be wooden, but I'm not thick!

definitions.meaning: completes the saying 'I can't add, but I can spell', the last words run together

definitions.text: I may be wooden, but I'm not thick!
definitions.meaning: a ..., or spillikin, is a thin strip of wood used in the game of jackstraws

explanation.surface: Two boasts: a poor arithmetician who can still do something, and a dull block who claims not to be stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' and 'thick' look like insults about dimness but describe a slender wooden stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellican is an old variant of spillikin, a slim splinter of wood picked from a heap in a game.

clue.text: Language in Italy, except for extreme parts, going back

indicators.note: the letters kept are then read in the opposite direction, right to left
the answer sits within the phrase in Italy, its outer letters at each end left out

explanation.surface: A language spoken in Italy, apart from the far ends of the country, is in retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for extreme parts' drops the I and Y at the ends of 'in Italy', leaving NITAL; 'going back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of ancient Rome is a classic example of a language.

clue.text: Dodgy nun with pi discourse thought to be guilty maybe

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or shifty, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shady nun and a pious lecture leave someone looking guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' shuffles NUN, PI and DISCOURSE together; 'pi' looks like the Greek letter or 'pious' but is just two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A person suspected of wrongdoing is said to be held in suspicion before guilt is proved.

clue.text: Like something a twister could get his hands on?

definitions.text: Like something a twister could get his hands on?

parts.words: Like something a twister could get his hands on?
parts.note: a twister turns things round, so an object he could turn is capable of being spun

explanation.surface: Sounds like a con man eyeing up something to swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twister' suggests a cheat or a tornado, but here is just someone who twists.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to be turned about an axis, which is what a twisting person would do.

clue.text: Non-editorial matter to which editor gets referred

parts.note: an advert is paid material in a paper, not written by the editorial staff

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is pointed to the advertising pages.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to something is to call attention to it or mention it, much as one refers.

clue.text: The general situation on their feet?

definitions.meaning: the state of affairs at present
read literally, things that are standing are upright

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: objects that stand are on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the current state of affairs, and literally describes upright things.

clue.text: Old woman, say, getting upset — being too old

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: eg (for example) is what say means here

explanation.surface: An old lady gets upset at being told she is past it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman, say' reads as one picture of a grandmother, but splits three ways. 'getting upset' reverses its piece, as fits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Over age means exceeding the age limit, in this sense too old.

clue.text: Report from a noble fellow with a stutter

indicators.note: a stutter repeats the opening sound, so the first letter of the noble's title is said twice

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
a count is a European nobleman

explanation.surface: A report received from a stammering aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a narrative or description of events.

clue.text: Way seaman shows pity

parts.note: a path is a way or track
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: Someone's way of life as a sailor reveals compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that arouses sympathy or sorrow.

clue.text: Expert in a warehouse missing nothing

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for nothing is taken away

parts.note: a depot is a storage building
O stands for zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A skilled worker in a storehouse who never loses anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adept is highly skilled, a synonym of expert.

clue.text: Excessively stupid chat by the fellow — mouthy problem

parts.note: too means to an excessive degree

indicators.note: stupid suggests the word chat is muddled into a new order

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a male, the fellow

explanation.surface: A man's foolish talk is far too much for a gobby troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges CHAT to THAC. 'Mouthy' usually means cheeky, but here it means in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in a tooth is a trouble located in the mouth, hence the playful adjective.

clue.text: Residence in hospital north of river

indicators.note: in a down clue north of means above, so the hospital letter comes first

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A home that is in a hospital up the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a building people live in, a dwelling.

clue.text: Alice maybe to perform as lead singer?

definitions.meaning: an Alice band is a style of hairband, named after Alice in Wonderland
a lead singer might be said to head a band, fronting the group

explanation.walkthrough: 'Alice' looks like a person but is the Alice band, a kind of hair accessory.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip worn round the head to hold hair back; an Alice band is one example.

clue.text: Grand time to take a holiday?

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means dignified, imposing
a summer month, when many people go away on vacation

explanation.walkthrough: The capital G hides the adjective; the second sense is the month, a peak vacation time.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic and awe-inspiring describes the adjective; the eighth month is the noun.

clue.text: Like some meat needing weeks for preparation, then barely cooked

indicators.note: preparation suggests the letters of weeks are made ready in a new order

parts.note: rare meat is still red inside

explanation.surface: Meat that needs weeks of preparation and then is served rare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for preparation' rearranges WEEKS into SKEWE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kebab meat is pierced on a spit before grilling, so it is pierced through in this way.

clue.text: Magnificent group? A bit trendy to begin with

indicators.note: the trendy word comes first, starting the answer before the bit

parts.note: hep is old slang for fashionable, like hip
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: A splendid band that was only somewhat fashionable at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magnificent' alludes to the film The Magnificent Seven, so the group has seven members.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptad is a set of seven, like the seven gunmen of the Western.
